slides.headline: Thirty Bodies, Dynamited Before Dawn
slides.body: August 20, 1976. An explosion outside Buenos Aires scattered thirty corpses across a field. The dictatorship called it terrorism.

slides.headline: Five Months Into the Junta
slides.body: Jorge Videla seized Argentina in March 1976. Twenty men and ten women were already held inside a Federal Police building.

slides.headline: Bound, Blindfolded, Shot in the Skull
slides.body: Police drove them to Fatima, in Pilar, and shot each from under a meter away. Then they detonated the bodies.

slides.headline: The CIA Named the Killers
slides.body: A CIA cable reported the thirty were killed under Federal Police detention. Washington knew within five days of the blast.
slides.source: National Security Archive, CIA cable, Aug 1976

slides.headline: Five Still Have No Name
slides.body: Forensic anthropologists matched relatives' blood to bone fragments for fifty years. Twenty-five victims now have names. Five are still waiting.

slides.headline: Two Convicted. Thirty Executed.
slides.body: Only two police commissioners were sentenced to life, in 2008. Thirty people died that night. Who else walked away?
